newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rebound with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rebound with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Monday, following the rebound in U.S. Treasuries after the fall-out Friday in reaction to statements by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

"The market recuperated, it was more or less just following international markets," said a trader at a large foreign bank. Activity was fairly busy around noon but calmed down in the afternoon, market players said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.35 to 122.60, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 86.

Separately, talk by London traders that Argentina could issue a jumbo mark Eurobond before yearend of between 750 million and 1.0 billion marks at a five- or 10-year maturity continued the sustained pace of issuance announcements that has underpinned the market recently.
On Tuesday, the government is due to sell $500 million of two-year Bontes, or treasury bonds, which will be an important gauge of the government's ability to find financing in the local market.
"The market is looking for support and is still continuing in an upward channel," said an analyst.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.38 percent from 6.40 percent.
